body:
This is related to a discussion that happened [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/99534), and resulted in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102440 which may end up in Godot 4.5.

If PR #102440 _does_ get merged, then checking if something is exposed should be equivalent to `ClassDB::can_instantiate()`. In that case, maybe we don't need to expose `is_class_exposed()`?

> This is related to a discussion that happened [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/99534), and resulted in #102440 which may end up in Godot 4.5.
> 
> If PR #102440 _does_ get merged, then checking if something is exposed should be equivalent to `ClassDB::can_instantiate()`. In that case, maybe we don't need to expose `is_class_exposed()`?

I did some testing, the problem with using `ClassDB.can_instantiate()` is that it checks for `p_class_info->creation_func` (its main objective) and it will filter out classes that are exposed, have documentation and doesn't throw any errors in the GDScript side.

I think having access to `is_class_exposed` should make the use of both methods more predictable and granular. One checks for availability and the other for the ability to instantiate.
